title: Protecting Data

header.html: 3.3 Summarize concepts and strategies used to protect data
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

html:
1Data types and states

Group Items Meaning
Data types Structured Organized in fields such as a database table
Unstructured No fixed format: documents, email, images, video
Data states Data at rest Stored (disk, database, backup): protect with encryption and access control
Data in use Being processed in memory: protect with access control and secure processing
Data in transit Moving over a network: protect with TLS, VPN, IPsec

Exam tip

. At rest = stored (encrypt the disk or database). In transit = moving (TLS or VPN). In use = in memory (hardest to protect).

2Data classification

Classification labels data by how sensitive it is, so it gets the right level of protection.

Label Typical meaning
Public Safe to share with anyone
Restricted Limited to specific groups
Confidential Harm if disclosed outside the company
Sensitive Needs care: for example personal or financial data
Secret / Top secret Government-style high levels: serious or grave damage if exposed
Critical Essential to operations: loss halts the business

Organizations choose their own scheme; the key is applying handling rules to each level.

3Methods used to secure data

Method Meaning Reversible?
Encryption Scrambles data with a key Yes, with the key
Hashing One-way fingerprint No
Masking Hides part of a value (****-1234) No (display only)
Tokenization Replaces a value with a random token; the real value is in a secure vault Yes, through the vault
Obfuscation Makes data hard to understand Often weak
Deidentification Removes personal identifiers Not meant to be
Filtering Blocks or removes sensitive content from data flows n/a
Data transpose Rearranges data (for example swapping fields) Depends

Exam tip

. Tokenization swaps the value for a token stored with a vault; it is common for payment cards. Masking is display protection. Hashing cannot be reversed. Deidentification supports privacy.

4Data protection roles

Role Responsibility
Data owner Accountable for the data; decides classification and access
Data custodian Operates and protects the data day to day (technical controls, backups)
Data steward Ensures data quality and proper use under policy
Data operator Processes data on instructions
Data controller Decides why and how personal data is processed
Data subprocessor A third party that processes data for a processor

5Data handling and life cycle

Topic Items
Handling Endpoints, marking and labeling, geofencing (limit by location), data location, data placement
Life cycle Creation, management, distribution, retention, disposal
Compliance Standards, health data, personal information, financial, child or minor data, intellectual property, legal data
Exam tip

. Disposal must be secure (shredding, cryptographic erase, degaussing). The data owner classifies; the custodian implements controls. A controller decides purposes; a processor acts on its behalf.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants to keep real card numbers out of its order system but still allow refunds. Which method fits best?

  • AHashing
  • BSalting
  • CTokenization
  • DDeidentification
Show the answer

Answer: C. Tokenization replaces the card number with a token while the real value stays in a secure vault for authorized use.

S2A call center screen shows only the last four digits of a card. Which method is this?

  • AEncryption
  • BMasking
  • CFiltering
  • DSteganography
Show the answer

Answer: B. Showing part of a value and hiding the rest is masking.

S3Customer files on a laptop are encrypted with full disk encryption. Which data state does this protect?

  • AData in use
  • BData in transit
  • CData at rest
  • DData in memory
Show the answer

Answer: C. Stored data is data at rest, and disk encryption protects it.

S4Who decides how a company's customer database is classified and who may access it?

  • AData custodian
  • BData subprocessor
  • CData operator
  • DData owner
Show the answer

Answer: D. The data owner is accountable for the data and sets its classification and access rules.

S5An administrator backs up and secures the database servers according to the owner's rules. Which role is this?

  • AData custodian
  • BData controller
  • CData steward
  • DData owner
Show the answer

Answer: A. The custodian operates and protects the data using technical controls.

S6A company restricts who can download files depending on the country they are in. Which handling technique is this?

  • ATokenization
  • BSalting
  • CData transpose
  • DGeofencing
Show the answer

Answer: D. Geofencing limits access or use based on location.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Name the three data states.

Show the answer

At rest, in use and in transit.

R2What is the difference between structured and unstructured data?

Show the answer

Structured data has fixed fields; unstructured data has no fixed format.

R3Which method is reversible only through a vault?

Show the answer

Tokenization.

R4What is the data steward responsible for?

Show the answer

Data quality and proper use under policy.

R5Name the five stages of the data life cycle.

Show the answer

Creation, management, distribution, retention and disposal.

R6What is a data controller?

Show the answer

The party that decides why and how personal data is processed.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
States at rest (stored), in use (memory), in transit (network)
Classification public, restricted, confidential, sensitive, secret, top secret, critical
Methods encryption, hashing, masking, tokenization (vault), obfuscation, deidentification, filtering, transpose
Roles owner (accountable), custodian (operates), steward (quality), operator, controller, subprocessor
Handling labeling, geofencing, location, placement; life cycle ends with secure disposal
